editorial.marketOverview: Sunday US cash markets are closed, leaving Friday's Nasdaq -0.91%, QQQ -1.19% and SOX -3.4% as latest regular-session signals. SOX's reported +8.1% weekly gain tempers but does not negate the chip-led Friday decline. Elevated reported Treasury yields and concentrated AI-sector uncertainty sustain a bearish three-day bias with moderate confidence and very high event risk.
editorial.whatChanged: Reuters on November 15 reported interceptions of two Houthi missiles headed toward Riyadh and three drones over Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. This raises geopolitical attention because the region hosts energy infrastructure, but no new oil-production outage or market repricing is verified. It therefore increases monitoring priority, not the base-case path. Open Watch remains unchanged at 163 curated events.
editorial.marketInterpretation: A potential geopolitical oil shock could lift inflation and yield pressure, but extrapolating such an outcome from intercepted attacks alone would be speculative. Friday Brent settlement of $95.84 and an asynchronous WTI $88.57 are not current Sunday prices. Reported 10Y 5.133% and 2Y 4.850% imply a +28.3bp spread, not an independently synchronized closing curve. Missing volatility, breadth and FedWatch readings constrain confidence.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday Nov 16: watch Empire State manufacturing, opening SOX versus QQQ, volatility, yields and whether energy futures react to Saudi news. Tuesday Nov 17: retail sales and industrial production can shift policy expectations before Nvidia's after-close results. Wednesday Nov 18: Nvidia's first cash-session reaction, housing starts and 14:00 ET FOMC minutes can determine bearish continuation or a relief rebound. All paths remain conditional, not observed outcomes.
editorial.bullCase: Semiconductor leadership stabilizes, Nasdaq participation broadens, Treasury yields ease and Nvidia delivers constructive guidance. No oil disruption following the reported interceptions would remove one emerging tail risk. SOX's weekly recovery and previous crude easing provide rebound potential.
editorial.bearCase: Renewed SOX underperformance, wider negative breadth, rising VXN/VIX and higher 10Y yields could magnify downside. Disappointing Nvidia guidance or verified disruption to Gulf energy infrastructure would add pressure, but neither is an established outcome at this checkpoint.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Saudi incident consequences against primary and Reuters reporting and check live Brent/WTI only when reliably timestamped. On Monday obtain synchronized QQQ/Nasdaq, SOX, VXN/VIX, breadth, Treasury 10Y/2Y and direct FedWatch, then compare with curated Open Watch additions. Confirm Nvidia reporting timing and separate anticipated impact from observed reaction.
